stem: A team wants to test whether a page supports reflow at the width WCAG 2.2 expects. Which viewport should they test?

options.rationale: WCAG's reflow criterion uses 320 CSS pixels, the equivalent of 400% zoom on a 1280-pixel-wide viewport.

options.text: A 768 CSS pixel wide tablet viewport at default zoom.
options.rationale: A tablet width does not test the reflow requirement.

options.text: A 1280 CSS pixel wide desktop viewport at 200% zoom.
options.rationale: 200% zoom at 1280 pixels gives 640 CSS pixels, not the 320-pixel width used for reflow.

options.text: The narrowest width the design team supports in its browser matrix.
options.rationale: The criterion sets the test width, a support matrix does not replace it.

explanation: WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 1.4.10 Reflow expects content to work at a width equivalent to 320 CSS pixels, which corresponds to 400% zoom on a 1280-pixel-wide viewport. At that width, content should not require two-dimensional scrolling, apart from allowed exceptions such as data tables.

references.title: W3C WAI — Understanding Success Criterion 1.4.10: Reflow
